title: Pin criterion baselines for all targeted kernels
description:
Pin the current criterion baseline for every Tier A–D kernel and commit a JSON manifest mapping each kernel to its baseline name and measurement commit. This is the V0 reference against which every subsequent spiral step proves its gain.

## Background

The PPC methodology requires a stable, version-pinned baseline so before/after measurements compare against an immutable reference. The committed `target/criterion/` directory has recent runs (Apr 18–25, 2026) but no version-pinning. This task runs `cargo bench -p gf2-core --bench <kernel-bench> -- --save-baseline ppc-v0-2026-04-25` for every targeted bench and records the manifest at `dev/benchmarks/ppc-baselines.json`.

Benches to baseline: `matrix_vector` (A1), `matmul` (A2 and B3), `fp_specialized` + `fieldvec_dot_product` (A3, C3, C4, C5), `gf2m_mul_strategies` and `gf2m_wide_mul` (C1, C2), `m4rm_components` and `m4rm_profile` (B2, B3), `sparse` (D1, D2). The transpose kernel has no dedicated bench yet — B1 creates one before its first edit.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] `dev/benchmarks/ppc-baselines.json` exists, valid JSON, contains an entry for every Tier A–D kernel with `baseline_name`, `commit_hash`, `bench_target`, and design-size-class fields.
- [hard] All baselines exist under `target/criterion/<benchmark>/<baseline-name>/`.
- [hard] Re-running `cargo bench -p gf2-core --bench <bench> -- --baseline ppc-v0-2026-04-25` succeeds without modification.
